_comment: Fragment: one more domain-process call inside a bot command. Both skeletons
already carry the first call — use this to add a second (third, …) when a
command chains processes, e.g. auth -> lookup.
Splice the nodes into scheme.nodes and rewire to_node_id / err_node_id.
A namespaced key still has to be FORWARDED to be renderable: the final
Send Message api_copy is group:"" and carries only the fields named in
its data block, so "reg2_cardPassword": "{{reg2_cardPassword}}" must be
listed there or the chat shows a literal {{reg2_cardPassword}}.
THE NAMESPACING NODE IS NOT OPTIONAL WHEN A COMMAND MAKES 2+ CALLS.
An api_rpc callee's res_data merges into the CALLER's task data at top
level. Every process in this family replies with the same {result, code}
envelope, so the second callee silently overwrites the first one's verdict
and the command branches on the wrong outcome. With exactly one call there
is nothing to overwrite — read {{result}}/{{code}} directly and skip it.
It must be an api_code, NOT a set_param: lint-process cannot parse
JavaScript, so it resolves a set_param's outputs by scanning downstream
node configuration. A data.auth_result read inside a Code node is invisible
to it and the file fails with 'UNUSED SET_PARAM … but no downstream node
references them'. Same assignments, different node type.
The time semaphor is what stops a hung or paused callee from parking the
task forever — in a chat that means a user staring at nothing. 30 sec is
the server minimum (lint rejects lower), so it is also the floor on how
fast a command can fail: write the timeout copy to read sensibly after a
half-minute, not as a flicker.
Prefer @alias over a numeric conv_id when the callee has one: the numeric
id is stage-specific and does not survive a deploy-stage promotion.

_comment: For a domain process with NO reachable api_rpc_reply, api_rpc would hang
until the semaphor fires. Use api_copy instead and acknowledge only what
you actually know: the request was submitted. Do not render a
confirmation the backend never sent.
